"I Never rested on the Muses bed,
Nor dipt my pen in Poesy's well;
But as I rambled idly by,
Your haunts, dear Drummond, I did spy,
And thought I would try my skill
To sing your praise, and make you ill."

This is the dedicatory poem "To William Drummond of Hawthornden" by M.M., where the original source texts have been lost. The poem is written in a humble tone, expressing that the author did not rest on the Muses' bed (a metaphor for being inspired by the muses) and did not dip his pen in Poesy's well (a metaphor for being skilled in poetry). Despite this, the author saw Drummond's haunts and decided to try writing a poem to praise him, acknowledging that it might make Drummond ill.
